articles.title: Youth: Sharon Horgan’s comedy about dating at 50 is utterly hilarious
articles.description: The perils of ageing and the horrors of finding post-divorce romance are laid bare in the new show from the creator of Motherland. It’s humungously funny, and so acutely observed it’s painful Ageing has changed, hasn’t it? There’s a generation of middle-aged and perimenopausal elder millennials and xennials who refuse to do it. We’re young enough to be part of an online world that puts a premium on appearance, too old for such narcissistic self-branding to be achieved without unsustainable effort. Dating apps and social media connect people across generations, so it’s easy to become confused about how old we actually are. Here’s a tip: ask your knees. This brings us to Youth (from Monday 21 Sepptember, HBO Max), Sharon Horgan ���s dramedy about being 50. That perky title is a quip about the decade being known as “the youth of old age”. Horgan is Alex, a divorcee in her sandwich years, caring for teenage son Ruarí and ageing parents. There’s a lot going on in her life, and some doom. She’s falling forwards in a semi-successful career as a literary agent, getting back into dating under pressure. She needs someone to fall in love with her immediately, as she points out to her best friend. Not for romantic myth-making, but “so there’s a bit of time with the present version of me, before the ‘old me’ is here”. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Weapons’ Director Returns With His Scariest Movie Yet
articles.description: Courtesy of Sony Pictures Not since John Carpenter has a horror director burst onto the scene like Zach Cregger, whose first two films, Barbarian and the Oscar-winning Weapons , established him as a generational scary-movie talent, and whose third—and best—feature, Resident Evil , solidifies his status as a maestro of monstrous madness. A PlayStation adaptation that’s at once spiritually faithful to its source material and yet unburdened by demands for across-the-board fidelity—a tack that was also taken by Paul W. Anderson and Milla Jovovich’s wholly separate six-entry series—Cregger’s latest (Sept. 18, in theaters) is less formally adventurous than his prior behind-the-camera efforts, opting for a pedal-to-the-metal dash into a heart of malevolent darkness. As hilarious as it is unnerving, it’s the rare video game-based film to rock from breakneck start to insane finish. Read more at The Daily Beast.

articles.title: V For Vendetta 20th Anniversary - Official ‘Tickets on Sale’ Trailer
articles.description: Freedom! Forever! Tickets now on sale for V for Vendetta 20th Anniversary, returning to theatres nationwide November 1 & 5. Stand with V & get tickets now: https://hubs.la/Q04v86P70 #VforVendetta #VforVendetta20 Based on the groundbreaking DC Vertigo graphic novel and produced by the Wachowskis, V for Vendetta (2006) became an instant classic, inspiring a generation with its message of defiance and freedom. Set against the futuristic landscape of totalitarian Britain, V for Vendetta tells the story of a young working-class woman named Evey, played by Natalie Portman, who is rescued from a life-and-death situation by a masked man known only as “V,” played by Hugo Weaving. V for Vendetta also stars Stephen Rea and John Hurt. The film is directed by James McTeigue, produced by Joel Silver, Grant Hill and The Wachowskis from a screenplay by The Wachowskis, based on the graphic novel illustrated by David Lloyd and published by DC Comics. The 20th anniversary theatrical event also features Freedom Forever, an exclusive featurette with director James McTeigue reflecting on the films and art that shaped V for Vendetta, the enduring mythology of V, and why its ideas of freedom, identity and resistance continue to resonate today. Warner Bros. Pictures presents, in association with Virtual Studios, a Silver Pictures production in association with Anarchos Productions Inc., V for Vendetta. The film returns to theatres nationwide November 1 & 5, presented by Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group, Saga Arts and Fathom Entertainment.
